summary.text: A 32-year-old Chinese female hepatitis B virus carrier started minocycline 50 mg twice daily and vitamin B6 for acne. About one week after starting these drugs she presented with loss of appetite, fatigue, and yellowing of the skin and sclera, with yellow urine and bloating. Liver and kidney tests one month before admission were reported, and she denied other medications and had no history of hypertension, diabetes, or drug allergies.

She was afebrile with a pulse of 104 beats/min, dark yellow skin and scleral icterus. Abdominal CT showed fatty liver, cirrhosis and possible liver nodules; ultrasound showed peritoneal effusion and gallbladder wall edema. AST, ALT, ALP and bilirubin were significantly elevated with prolonged prothrombin time, fibrinogen 0.75 g/L, positive hepatitis B markers and low complement. The final diagnosis was subacute liver failure with chronic hepatitis B.

Minocycline was discontinued and symptomatic and liver enzyme protection treatment was started. Coagulation function reached critical values, and she received twelve blood transfusions including frozen fresh plasma and cryoprecipitate with coagulation factor supplementation. Because her blood type complicated plasma matching for plasmapheresis, DPMAS with renal replacement therapy was used, with three DPMAS treatments on the third, fourth and sixth days after admission. The abstract describes artificial liver therapy combined with CRRT.

Coagulation, liver and kidney function gradually returned to near-normal levels and she was discharged in stable condition. ALT fell substantially with a shift to a cholestatic pattern, coagulation indices remained above the upper limit and bilirubin stayed elevated. The case was classified as probable drug-induced liver injury with RUCAM 7 and Naranjo 6.
